about: T01 voiceover script for ElevenLabs (female tutor voice, warm, clear, unhurried). Each line is generated as its own clip and placed at film time t (seconds). say = spoken form when it differs from text.

lines.text: Lesson one: what is cryptocurrency? Let's start at the very beginning.
You've probably seen a screen like this. Prices that never sit still.
BTC keeps moving. But what is BTC, really? By the end of this lesson, you'll know.
Let's start with money. Money is value that people agree to accept.
You hand it over, and you get food, a bus ticket, or rent paid.
And most money today is already just numbers, stored in a bank's computers.
Value is what something is worth to people. Money is a shared way to store and exchange it.
A digital asset is anything of value that exists only as digital records.
A bank balance. Points in a game. Airline miles.
Cryptocurrency is one kind of digital asset, like BTC and ETH. But not every digital asset is crypto.
Here's the key idea. Say a friend sends you a small amount of crypto.
The payment is written into a shared record, called a ledger.
Many computers around the world keep a copy, and they check each other.
The records are grouped into blocks, linked in order. That's the blockchain.
So there's no bank in the middle. The network keeps the record.
Meet Bitcoin, symbol B T C: the first and best-known cryptocurrency.
It launched in 2009, and no more than twenty-one million bitcoin can ever exist.
One bitcoin can be split into tiny parts, so you can own a small piece, like 0.002 BTC.
lines.say: One bitcoin can be split into tiny parts, so you can own a small piece, like zero point zero zero two B T C.

lines.text: Here's a common mistake. There is no coin inside your phone.
A wallet holds keys, which prove you control your crypto. The coins themselves are entries on the blockchain.
On an exchange, the exchange holds the keys for you. Lose your keys, and you can lose access.
Two words you'll hear: coins and tokens. A coin runs on its own blockchain.
A token is built on top of an existing one. USDT is a token designed to track the US dollar.
lines.say: A token is built on top of an existing one. U S D T is a token designed to track the US dollar.

lines.text: Now a worked example. What is my BTC worth?
Say you hold 0.002 BTC, and one BTC costs 60,000 USDT.
lines.say: Say you hold zero point zero zero two B T C, and one B T C costs sixty thousand U S D T.

lines.text: Amount times price: 120 USDT. That's all it is.
lines.say: Amount times price: one hundred and twenty U S D T. That's all it is.

lines.text: Now watch what happens when the price moves.
The price rises to 63,000. Your value rises to 126.
lines.say: The price rises to sixty-three thousand. Your value rises to one hundred and twenty-six.

lines.text: Then it falls to 57,000. Your value falls to 114.
lines.say: Then it falls to fifty-seven thousand. Your value falls to one hundred and fourteen.

lines.text: Notice: you still hold the same 0.002 BTC. Only its value changed.
lines.say: Notice: you still hold the same zero point zero zero two B T C. Only its value changed.

lines.text: Your turn. You hold 0.002 BTC, and the price is 65,000 USDT. What is it worth? Pause if you need more time.
lines.say: Your turn. You hold zero point zero zero two B T C, and the price is sixty-five thousand U S D T. What is it worth? Pause if you need more time.

lines.text: The answer: 130 USDT. Well done if you got it.
lines.say: The answer: one hundred and thirty U S D T. Well done if you got it.

lines.text: Quick check: crypto, or not crypto?
Bitcoin: crypto. Game points: not crypto. Ether: crypto. A bank balance: not crypto.
And USDT? It counts too. It's a crypto token.
lines.say: And U S D T? It counts too. It's a crypto token.

lines.text: Before you go further, know the risks.
No government stands behind crypto. If something goes wrong, nobody has to pay you back.
Prices can rise or fall a lot in a single day.
Lose your keys, or get tricked by a scammer, and your crypto can be gone for good.
And owning BTC is not the same as trading futures, which are contracts about its price. We'll cover those later.
Learn first, and never risk money you can't afford to lose.
Let's recap.
Cryptocurrency is a digital asset recorded on a shared blockchain.
A wallet holds keys. The coins live on the blockchain.
And value equals amount times price. The amount stays; the value moves.
Check yourself: if BTC falls ten percent, what happens to your 0.002 BTC?
lines.say: Check yourself: if B T C falls ten percent, what happens to your zero point zero zero two B T C?

lines.text: You still hold 0.002 BTC. Its value falls by ten percent.
lines.say: You still hold zero point zero zero two B T C. Its value falls by ten percent.

lines.text: Great start! Next up: why do crypto prices move? See you in lesson two.
